reasons: Classification is correct: Section 14.1 provides a RevMed indemnity only for its misconduct and its breaches of reps/warranties/obligations, with no head for third-party IP infringement claims, and Section 14.2(a) affirmatively pushes claims arising from Sanofi's Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization onto us. Under the detection guidance ('Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement') this fails the fallback (which requires a Vendor IP indemnity), so a deviation rather than a compliant-at-fallback finding is appropriate; the knowledge-qualified, Execution-Date-only Article XIII IP warranties do not substitute.

Redline is valid and near-minimal: a new subsection (d) inserted after 14.1(c), with the conforming update of the carve-out cross-reference from '(a) through (c)' to '(a) through (d)' (changed-character ratio 0.053). It preserves RevMed's existing exceptions for Sanofi's own negligence and breaches and uses 'notwithstanding Section 14.2(a)' to resolve the conflict with our own indemnity rather than rewriting Section 14.2.

The failed deterministic check 'vendor indemnity for IP infringement present' is a phrasing artefact, not a substantive gap: the inserted (d) expressly covers Third Party Claims alleging that the licensed technology or the Products 'infringes or misappropriates any Patent Right or other intellectual property right of a Third Party', which is the playbook's core requirement.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice; it states what changed, why (licensor should stand behind IP claims on the technology it licenses), and notes that RevMed's existing carve-outs remain.

Minor, non-fatal observations only: the inserted head is somewhat broader than the model language (it reaches Sanofi-conducted Development/Commercialization) and omits the fallback's customary exclusions (Customer modifications/combinations/specifications) and any super-cap; these are opening-position asks that favour our client and do not make the edit directionally wrong or unactionable.
